reshared_post.author_headline: Lead GenAI Engineer at Trimble | Founder & Creator of Ponytail
reshared_post.reshared_text:
Ever met a senior dev whose entire personality is "do we even need to build this?" I packaged that guy into a plugin.

Meet ponytail, lazy-senior-dev mode for your coding agent. It writes the least code that actually works, then stops.

The goal isn't to write as little code as possible, but to write only what is necessary.

Benchmarked across multiple real tasks against a no-skill agent and Caveman (the other minimalist skill):
• A seventh of the code: 490 lines vs 3,629 no-skill, and a third of Caveman's 1,440
• 47% fewer tokens, 3x faster than no-skill
• 100% on every security and concurrency probe, same as everyone
• Surprise feature request? ponytail added it in 96 lines. Caveman needed 413. No-skill: 1,115.

Lazy, not negligent: trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security, and accessibility are never on the chopping block.

"What if I really need the 120-line cache class?" You don't. Insist anyway and he'll build it. Slowly. Correctly. While looking at you.

"Does it scale?" The code you never wrote scales infinitely. Zero bugs, zero CVEs, 100% uptime since forever. The 3,139 lines nobody wrote have never caused an incident.

Every shortcut it takes is marked with a ponytail: comment naming its upgrade path.

The best code really is the code you never wrote.

Steal it here: https://lnkd.in/e7ZeuBFB
